solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hoping to gain, lay out trendy underwear

parts.note: a vest is a sleeveless undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out on fashionable underwear in the hope of impressing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to put money into something expecting a profitable return later.

clue.text: Architect Jones includes a bit of dark colour

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it inside itself

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the seventeenth-century English architect

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small part of it, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A famous architect's design features a touch of deep, sombre colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones designed the Banqueting House in London; his first name wraps the opening letter of dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet shade, one of the traditional seven hues of the rainbow.

clue.text: Nasty cleric involved in spurious type of reasoning

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters get twisted up

explanation.surface: A spiteful priest gets mixed up in some dodgy logic.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is circular argument, where a conclusion is used to prove its own premise.

clue.text: Worker with horses less happy about foal's backside

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
a backside is the rear end, so only the final letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A stable hand is gloomier still about a young horse's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes and repairs saddles and harness, a craftsman serving riders and their mounts.

clue.text: Violent lashes creating trouble

indicators.note: violent suggests things thrown about wildly, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A savage whipping causes problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is bother or annoying difficulty, an informal word for aggravation.

clue.text: Jelly with a distinctive flavour mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: spice gives food a distinctive flavour

explanation.surface: A savoury jelly with a strongly characteristic taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a clear savoury gelatine made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Put an end to dubious practices in sport

parts.note: to squash something is to suppress it

explanation.surface: A call to stamp out cheating and corruption in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash rackets is the full formal name of the indoor game of squash, played against walls.

clue.text: Reveal truth about former model

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A tabloid spills the beans on someone's ex, a one-time model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun but is the verb, to sit for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose a scandal is to make public hidden wrongdoing or secrets.

clue.text: Key match has editor turning to drink

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
cider is a drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Before a crucial game, the editor takes to the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is the game played to settle a tied contest, the one that determines the winner.

clue.text: Put down leader, get excited

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urges the crowd to topple their chief and get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegated means demoted or consigned to a lower rank, as a team dropping a division.

clue.text: Fruit soft and chubby

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A description of some fruit: soft and plump-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes someone pleasantly rounded or slightly fat in build.

clue.text: Get bigger with added pounds and grumble noisily

parts.note: to grow is to increase in size
L is the symbol for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone who has put on weight complains loudly about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To growl is to make a low guttural sound of anger or complaint.

clue.text: Place across street for insects

indicators.note: a word lying across another spans it, so it sits around it

parts.note: locus is Latin for a place or position
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Somewhere over the road is good for finding bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are swarming grasshoppers that devastate crops, so they are a kind of insect.

clue.text: Good person left in game — one making progress slowly?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: rugger is British slang for rugby union
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A decent sort left out on the pitch, plodding along slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugger is the public-school nickname for rugby union. The question mark flags a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggler battles with difficulty, so advances only with effort and little speed.

clue.text: I am sick, upset, over relation in naughty relationship

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above what follows
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the words read bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
a son is a family relation

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell and upset about a relative's illicit affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison can mean a secret sexual affair, especially an adulterous one.

clue.text: In the same place I stay overlooking Malta's capital

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means sitting above what follows
a capital is a head letter, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker stays at a spot with views of Valletta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malta's capital' looks like Valletta; here it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin term used in footnotes to cite the source quoted just before.

clue.text: Said to have begun losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: to have started is to have begun

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to have become discouraged after a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or expressed in words, the past tense of speaking.

clue.text: Danger in chancy operation offering meat

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

explanation.surface: A hazardous gamble somehow ends up serving beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, usually braised or slow cooked.

clue.text: Monk ultimately 'urt, meeting a religious destiny

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter is wanted

parts.note: hurt is harm, and the apostrophe drops the H as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: A wounded monk accepts his religious fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'urt shows a dropped H, so the synonym loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma, in Hindu and Buddhist belief, is the force of past actions shaping future fate.

clue.text: Maybe a Glaswegian's course

parts.note: a Glaswegian is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man from Glasgow is taking his own route.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England; 'Maybe' signals that a Glaswegian is one kind of Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous racecourse hosting Royal Ascot, so it is a horse-racing track.

clue.text: Ornamentation found in wide corridor

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are lodged inside the next words

explanation.surface: Decorative features spotted along a broad hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the furnishing and decorative style of a room or building.

clue.text: Kind to carry son in downward journey

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A caring parent carries a boy on the way down a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a movement downwards, such as going down a mountain.

clue.text: Frenzied female, awfully mean, with a daughter

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wild, nasty woman and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a female follower of Dionysus, given to ecstatic frenzy in his rites.

clue.text: New university attracting silly nudes

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: silly means foolish or daft, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A fresh university campus draws in some naked models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New university' reads as one phrase, but New is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused means never used, fresh, still in its original untouched condition.
